Its frozen Lean type, prose statement and title are byte-identical to the comparator-accepted DAG node root.rectifiability-a1.density_comparison-a1, declaration Submission.rectifiability_density_comparison, which is reused rather than re-proved (no new worker). Its accepted natural-language proof follows verbatim.

Source: Simon, Ch. 1, Theorem 3.3 and its printed proof (p. 15) with A₁ := A and A₂ := V, using the 5-times covering lemma 3.4 and Corollary 3.5. (SimonGMT formalizes exactly this argument: mul_simonHausdorff_le_of_le_dimensionalUpperDensity, together with dimensionalUpperDensity_inter_of_mem_nhds and simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure.)

1. Normalizations. The outer measure of ν (ν(S) = inf{ν(B) : B ⊇ S Borel}) is Borel regular and all Borel sets are ν-measurable (Carathéodory), as required in 3.3. Simon's Hausdorff measure Hⁿ (covers by sets C of diameter < δ with cost ω_n (diam C/2)ⁿ, then δ ↓ 0) coincides with μHE[n] as an outer measure on ℝ^P: both are the n-dimensional Hausdorff measure normalized to agree with Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (Simon Ch. 1, 2.8-2.10; SimonGMT simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure and simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure). Write Θ*ⁿ(ν, V, x) := limsup_{r↓0} ν(V ∩ B̄_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ) (Simon (3.1)).

2. Localization. If x ∈ A ⊆ V and V is open, there is R > 0 with B̄_R(x) ⊆ V, so ν(V ∩ B̄_r(x)) = ν(B̄_r(x)) for 0 < r < R and Θ*ⁿ(ν, V, x) = Θ*ⁿ(ν, x) ≥ t. So the hypothesis of 3.3 holds with A₁ = A ⊆ A₂ = V.

3. Trivial cases. If t = 0 or ν(V) = ∞ there is nothing to prove. If t = ∞, then the hypothesis holds with every real t′ > 0 in place of t, so by the case 0 < t′ < ∞ below t′ Hⁿ(A) ≤ ν(V) for all such t′; hence either Hⁿ(A) = 0 (and ∞·0 = 0 ≤ ν(V)) or ν(V) = ∞. So assume 0 < t < ∞ and ν(V) < ∞.

4. Printed proof of 3.3. Take τ ∈ (0, t), so Θ*ⁿ(ν, V, x) > τ for every x ∈ A. For δ > 0 let 𝓑 be the family of closed balls B̄_ρ(x) with x ∈ A, 0 < ρ < δ/2 and ν(V ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≥ τ ω_n ρⁿ. By the definition of the limsup, 𝓑 covers A finely. By the 5-times covering lemma 3.4 there is a pairwise disjoint subfamily 𝓑′ ⊆ 𝓑 such that every B ∈ 𝓑 meets some B′ ∈ 𝓑′ with diam B′ ≥ diam B/2, hence B is contained in the concentric ball B̂′ with 5 times the radius of B′. Since ν(V ∩ B) > 0 for B ∈ 𝓑 and, for finitely many disjoint B_1, …, B_N ∈ 𝓑′, Σ_j ν(V ∩ B_j) = ν(V ∩ ⋃_j B_j) ≤ ν(V) < ∞, the family 𝓑′ is countable, 𝓑′ = {B̄_{ρ_j}(x_j) : j ≥ 1}, and Σ_j ω_n ρ_jⁿ ≤ τ^{-1} Σ_j ν(V ∩ B̄_{ρ_j}(x_j)) ≤ τ^{-1} ν(V) < ∞. By Corollary 3.5, A ∖ ⋃_{j ≤ N} B̄_{ρ_j}(x_j) ⊆ ⋃_{j > N} B̄_{5ρ_j}(x_j) for every N. These balls have diameter < 5δ and a ball of radius ρ has cost ω_n (diam/2)ⁿ ≤ ω_n ρⁿ, so by the definition of Hⁿ_{5δ}: Hⁿ_{5δ}(A) ≤ Σ_{j ≤ N} ω_n ρ_jⁿ + 5ⁿ Σ_{j > N} ω_n ρ_jⁿ. Letting N → ∞ (the tail of a convergent series tends to 0) gives Hⁿ_{5δ}(A) ≤ Σ_j ω_n ρ_jⁿ ≤ τ^{-1} ν(V).

5. Letting δ ↓ 0 gives τ Hⁿ(A) ≤ ν(V), and letting τ ↑ t gives t Hⁿ(A) ≤ ν(V). By step 1 this is t·μHE[n](A) ≤ ν(V). (For n = 0 the same argument applies with ω_0 = 1 and ρ⁰ = 1.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Identify Simon's Hⁿ with μHE[n] (outer measures) and use Borel regularity of ν.
For x ∈ A ⊆ V with V open, Θ*ⁿ(ν, V, x) = Θ*ⁿ(ν, x) ≥ t, so Theorem 3.3 applies with A₁ = A, A₂ = V.
Dispose of t ∈ {0, ∞} and ν(V) = ∞.
Fine cover of A by balls with ν(V ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≥ τω_nρⁿ; the 5-times covering lemma gives a countable disjoint subfamily with Σ ω_nρ_jⁿ ≤ τ⁻¹ν(V).
Corollary 3.5 bounds Hⁿ_{5δ}(A) by the subfamily's cost; let δ ↓ 0 and τ ↑ t.

Its frozen Lean type, prose statement and title are byte-identical to the comparator-accepted DAG node root.slicing-a1.representation_unique-a1, declaration Submission.slicing_representation_unique, which is reused rather than re-proved (no new worker). Its accepted natural-language proof follows verbatim.

Conventions (as in the parent proof). D^k(U) is the space of test k-forms on U (smooth, compact support, tsupport ⊆ U; `TestFormOn U k`), D_k(U) the currents (`GeometricCurrentOn U k`: linear, and X(ω_j) → 0 whenever ω_j → 0 in D^k(U), i.e. all tsupports lie in one compact K ⊆ U and every iterated derivative of ω_j tends to 0 uniformly on K). I(k,P) is the set of strictly increasing β : {1,…,k} → {1,…,P}; e_β := (e_{β_1},…,e_{β_k}); dx^β is the coordinate k-covector, dx^β(e_γ) = δ_{βγ} for β, γ ∈ I(k,P). Fact A: every k-covector α equals Σ_β α(e_β) dx^β, and |α|² = Σ_β α(e_β)², where |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. A k-vector is a continuous linear functional w on k-covectors (`NVector`); put w^β := w(dx^β), so w(α) = Σ_β α(e_β) w^β and |w(α)| ≤ |α|·|w| with |w| := (Σ_β (w^β)²)^{1/2} (Cauchy–Schwarz). For a form ω, ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)|. M_W(X) = X.massOn W is the supremum of X(ω) over ω ∈ D^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. ρ_ε is a standard mollifier (smooth, ≥ 0, supported in the closed ε-ball, ∫ρ_ε = 1); for a continuous compactly supported form φ, ρ_ε*φ (componentwise convolution) is smooth, supported in the closed ε-neighbourhood of tsupport φ, satisfies |ρ_ε*φ(x)| ≤ ‖φ‖ (|·| is a norm, hence convex) and ρ_ε*φ → φ uniformly as ε ↓ 0. All measures are Borel measures on ℝ^P = Eucl P.

Source: the parent proof's preliminary R2 (uniqueness in Simon 2.7–2.9), stated locally on an open set W. Let P, k, U open, Borel measures μ₁, μ₂ on ℝ^P and maps v₁, v₂ : ℝ^P → (k-vectors) be such that x ↦ v_i(x)(ω(x)) is μ_i-integrable for every ω ∈ D^k(U) (i = 1, 2). Let W be open with ∫ v₁(ω) dμ₁ = ∫ v₂(ω) dμ₂ for all ω ∈ D^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Write v_i^β(x) := v_i(x)(dx^β). Fix a Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P and ω ∈ D^k(U) with K := tsupport ω ⊆ W.

1. (A neighbourhood of K.) K is compact and K ⊆ W ∩ U (test forms on U have tsupport ⊆ U), and W ∩ U is open. If K = ∅ then ω = 0 and both sides vanish; assume K ≠ ∅. Choose r > 0 such that the closed 2r-neighbourhood of K lies in W ∩ U; put W′ := {x : dist(x,K) < r} (open) and K_r := {x : dist(x,K) ≤ r} (compact, ⊇ closure W′, ⊆ W ∩ U).

2. (Local integrability.) Fix β ∈ I(k,P). Choose a smooth χ with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on K_r and tsupport χ a compact subset of {dist(·,K) < 2r} ⊆ W ∩ U, e.g. a mollified indicator function. The form x ↦ χ(x)dx^β is smooth with compact support and tsupport ⊆ U, i.e. it belongs to D^k(U); hence x ↦ v_i(x)(χ(x)dx^β) = χ(x)v_i^β(x) is μ_i-integrable. Therefore g_i^β := 1_{K_r}·v_i^β = 1_{K_r}·(χv_i^β) is μ_i-integrable (it is a.e.-strongly measurable as the product of an integrable function with the indicator of a closed set, and |g_i^β| ≤ |χv_i^β|).

3. (Agreement on smooth functions.) If φ is smooth with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ W′, then φdx^β ∈ D^k(U) has tsupport ⊆ W′ ⊆ W, so by hypothesis ∫ φv₁^β dμ₁ = ∫ φv₂^β dμ₂, i.e. ∫ φ g₁^β dμ₁ = ∫ φ g₂^β dμ₂ (φ vanishes off W′ ⊆ K_r).

4. (Agreement on continuous functions.) Let φ be continuous with compact support tsupport φ ⊆ W′, and s := dist(tsupport φ, ℝ^P ∖ W′) > 0 (s := 1 if W′ = ℝ^P). For 0 < ε < s/2, φ_ε := ρ_ε*φ is smooth with tsupport ⊆ {dist(·, tsupport φ) ≤ ε} ⊆ W′, |φ_ε| ≤ sup|φ|, and φ_ε → φ uniformly. By step 3, ∫ φ_ε g₁^β dμ₁ = ∫ φ_ε g₂^β dμ₂; dominated convergence (dominating functions sup|φ|·|g_i^β|) gives ∫ φ g₁^β dμ₁ = ∫ φ g₂^β dμ₂.

5. (Equality of measures on W′.) Define finite Borel measures λ₁(B) := ∫_B (g₁^β)⁺ dμ₁ + ∫_B (g₂^β)⁻ dμ₂ and λ₂(B) := ∫_B (g₁^β)⁻ dμ₁ + ∫_B (g₂^β)⁺ dμ₂. Step 4 says ∫ φ dλ₁ = ∫ φ dλ₂ for every continuous φ with compact support in W′. (i) For open O ⊆ ℝ^P, V := O ∩ W′ is open and φ_j(x) := min(1, max(0, j·dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ V) − 1))·max(0, min(1, j − |x|)) are continuous, compactly supported in V, 0 ≤ φ_j ≤ 1, and φ_j ↑ 1_V pointwise (if V = ℝ^P, which is possible only for P = 0, take the first factor ≡ 1); by monotone convergence λ₁(O ∩ W′) = λ₂(O ∩ W′). (ii) The finite measures B ↦ λ_i(B ∩ W′) agree on the π-system of open sets, which generates the Borel σ-algebra and contains ℝ^P; by the π–λ uniqueness theorem they agree on all Borel sets.

6. (Bounded Borel integrands.) Consequently ∫ h dλ₁ = ∫ h dλ₂ for every bounded Borel h vanishing off W′ (apply step 5 to simple functions and pass to uniform limits, separately for h⁺ and h⁻). Expanding λ₁, λ₂ (all terms are finite since g_i^β is integrable and h bounded) gives ∫ h g₁^β dμ₁ = ∫ h g₂^β dμ₂.

7. (Conclusion.) By Fact A, ω(x) = Σ_β ω_β(x) dx^β with ω_β(x) := ω(x)(e_β) continuous and vanishing off K ⊆ W′. Hence 1_A(x)v_i(x)(ω(x)) = Σ_β h_β(x) g_i^β(x) with h_β := 1_A ω_β, a bounded Borel function vanishing off K (on K ⊆ K_r, v_i^β = g_i^β). By step 6 for each β,

 This holds for every Borel A and every ω ∈ D^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Testing with χ dx^β (χ = 1 near K) shows g_i^β = 1_{K_r} v_i(dx^β) ∈ L¹(μ_i).

subproblems.title: Integrability of the integrands of τ(M, θ, ξ)
subproblems.statement:
Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, and let M ⊆ ℝ^P, θ : ℝ^P → ℝ, ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) (k-vectors, `NVector`) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ. Write H := Hᵏ = μHE[k].
(a) For every compact K ⊆ U and every k-covector b, the function x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(b) is H-integrable on M ∩ K.
(b) For every continuous k-covector field ω : ℝ^P → Λᵏ(ℝ^P) with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U, the function x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) is H-integrable on M.

Its frozen Lean type, prose statement and title are byte-identical to the comparator-accepted DAG node root.boundary_rectifiability-a1.local_to_global_im-a1.tau_integrable-a1, declaration Submission.ltg_tau_integrable, which is reused rather than re-proved (no new worker). Its accepted natural-language proof follows verbatim.

Source: facts (F0), (F2) and the remark 'All integrands are integrable' in step 7 of the parent proof, written out.

Notation. H := μHE[k]. For a k-covector α (a continuous alternating k-linear map), ‖α‖ is its operator norm, so |α(v₁,…,v_k)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_j |v_j|. The fields of IsRectifiableTriple used are nullMeasurableSet, integrableOn, aestronglyMeasurable and orients.

1. (Unit bound, F0.) For H⌞M-a.e. x and every k-covector α: |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖.
 By `orients`, for H⌞M-a.e. x there is an orthonormal τ : Fin k → ℝ^P with ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ. Since simpleNVector τ (α) = α(τ₁,…,τ_k), we get |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_j |τ_j| = ‖α‖, because |τ_j| = 1. For k = 0 the empty product is 1.

2. (Measurability.) Let ω : ℝ^P → Λᵏ be continuous. The evaluation map Λ_k × Λᵏ → ℝ, (w, α) ↦ w(α), is continuous. ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞M (`aestronglyMeasurable`), and ω is continuous. Hence x ↦ (ξ(x), ω(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞M, and so is its composition x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) with the evaluation map. The same holds for H⌞S whenever S ⊆ M, since H⌞S ≤ H⌞M. Taking ω constant equal to b gives the same for x ↦ ξ(x)(b).

3. (Part (a).) Let K ⊆ U be compact and b a k-covector.
 - By `integrableOn`, θ is H-integrable on M ∩ K.
 - Since M ∩ K ⊆ M, step 1 gives |ξ(x)(b)| ≤ ‖b‖ for H⌞(M ∩ K)-a.e. x.
 - By step 2, x ↦ ξ(x)(b) is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞(M ∩ K).
 The product of an integrable function with an a.e. strongly measurable, a.e. bounded function is integrable. So x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(b) is H-integrable on M ∩ K.

4. (Part (b) on the support.) Let ω be continuous with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U. Put K := tsupport ω, a compact subset of U.
 - Being continuous with compact support, ω is bounded: |ω(x)| ≤ C for all x, for some C.
 - θ is H-integrable on M ∩ K (`integrableOn`).
 - x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞(M ∩ K) (step 2), and |ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ C for H⌞(M ∩ K)-a.e. x (step 1).
 As in step 3, h(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) is H-integrable on M ∩ K.

5. (Part (b), conclusion.) If x ∈ M \ K, then x ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(x) = 0 and h(x) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(0) = 0. M is H-null-measurable (`nullMeasurableSet`) and M ∩ K ⊆ M. A function integrable on M ∩ K that vanishes on M \ (M ∩ K) is integrable on the null-measurable set M. Hence h is H-integrable on M. ∎

- Step 2: `Continuous.clm_apply continuous_fst continuous_snd`, composed via `Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable` with `hT.aestronglyMeasurable.prodMk hω.aestronglyMeasurable`. Note: `continuous_eval` fails, because the instance `ContinuousEval (NVector (Eucl P) k) (Covector (Eucl P) k) ℝ` is not found.
- Steps 3–4: `Integrable.bdd_mul`, together with `ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset inter_subset_left` and `AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure (Measure.restrict_mono inter_subset_left le_rfl)`. The bound C comes from `Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support`.
- Step 5: `IntegrableOn.of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero hT.nullMeasurableSet` and `image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport`.
- Do not use Integrable/IntegrableOn of NVector-valued functions: `ContinuousENorm (NVector (Eucl P) k)` does not synthesize.
proof_key_steps: Orientation (ξ = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τ_k with τ orthonormal) gives |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for H⌞M-a.e. x and every covector α.
x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable: continuous evaluation composed with (ξ, ω).
An integrable function (θ on M ∩ K) times an a.e.-bounded measurable factor is integrable. This gives (a), and gives (b) on M ∩ tsupport ω.
The integrand of (b) vanishes on M \ tsupport ω, so it is integrable on the null-measurable set M.

subproblems.title: Orthonormal frames of the same subspace have the same simple n-vector up to sign
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P be orthonormal families with span(range τ) = span(range τ'). Then simpleNVector τ' = simpleNVector τ or simpleNVector τ' = −simpleNVector τ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ τ' : Fin n → Eucl P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → Orthonormal ℝ τ' → Submodule.span ℝ (range τ) = Submodule.span ℝ (range τ') → simpleNVector τ' = simpleNVector τ ∨ simpleNVector τ' = -simpleNVector τ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused accepted declaration. Its frozen Lean type, prose statement and title are byte-identical to the comparator-accepted DAG node root.flat_iff_weak-a1.im_series-a1.frame_sign-a1, declaration Submission.fiw_ims_frame_sign, which is reused rather than re-proved (no new worker). Its accepted natural-language proof follows verbatim.

1. (Two orthonormal bases of Q.) Let Q := span(range τ) = span(range τ').
   - An orthonormal family is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so τ is a basis of Q (Basis.span).
   - It is orthonormal for the inner product of Q, which is the ambient one. Call this orthonormal basis b of Q (Basis.toOrthonormalBasis).
   - In the same way τ' is an orthonormal basis of span(range τ') = Q. Transporting along this equality of submodules gives an orthonormal basis b' of Q with b'_j = τ'_j.
   - In particular dim Q = n.

2. (Change of frame.) Let α be any n-covector on ℝ^P.
   - Its restriction f := α ∘ (inclusion Q ↪ ℝ^P), f(v_1, …, v_n) := α(v_1, …, v_n), is an alternating n-linear form on the n-dimensional space Q (AlternatingMap.compLinearMap with Q.subtype).
   - By AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det, f = f(b)·b.det.
   - Evaluating at b': α(τ') = f(b') = f(b)·b.det(b') = d·α(τ), where d := b.det(b') does not depend on α.
   - Elementary version: τ'_j = Σ_i O_{ij} τ_i with O_{ij} = ⟨τ_i, τ'_j⟩, because τ'_j ∈ Q and τ is an orthonormal basis of Q. Multilinearity and alternation give α(τ') = det(O)·α(τ), and d = det O.

3. (d = ±1.) b.det(b') is the determinant of the change-of-basis matrix between the orthonormal bases b and b' of Q. That matrix is orthogonal, so d = 1 or d = −1 (OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real). Elementary version: OᵀO = I because τ' is orthonormal, so d² = 1.

4. (Conclusion.)
   - For every α: (simpleNVector τ')(α) = α(τ') = d·α(τ) = (d • simpleNVector τ)(α) (simpleNVector_apply).
   - By extensionality of continuous linear maps, simpleNVector τ' = d • simpleNVector τ. This is simpleNVector τ if d = 1 and −simpleNVector τ if d = −1.
   - For n = 0 both families are empty, Q = 0, d = 1, and both sides are evaluation at the empty tuple. ∎
proof_key_steps: τ and τ' are orthonormal bases of the same n-dimensional subspace Q
restrict α to Q: α(τ') = b.det(b')·α(τ) by AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det
b.det(b') = ±1 since the change of basis between orthonormal bases is orthogonal
extensionality: simpleNVector τ' = ±simpleNVector τ

subproblems.title: Orientations of two rectifiable triples agree up to sign on the overlap of the carriers
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, H := μHE[n] on ℝ^P, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, and let (M₁, θ₁, ξ₁) and (M₂, θ₂, ξ₂) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple U n. Assume that for H-a.e. x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ (i.e. H.restrict(M₁ ∩ M₂)-a.e.), every subspace Q that is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M₁, θ₁) at x is also a weighted approximate tangent space of (M₂, θ₂) at x. Then for H-a.e. x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂, ξ₁(x) = ξ₂(x) or ξ₁(x) = −ξ₂(x).

Reused accepted declaration. Its frozen Lean type, prose statement and title are byte-identical to the comparator-accepted DAG node root.flat_iff_weak-a1.im_series-a1.orientation_sign-a1, declaration Submission.fiw_ims_orientation_sign, which is reused rather than re-proved (no new worker). Its accepted natural-language proof follows verbatim.

Let μ := H.restrict(M₁ ∩ M₂) and s(τ) := simpleNVector τ.

1. (Points of the overlap.) M₁ ∩ M₂ is H-null-measurable (field nullMeasurableSet of both triples, NullMeasurableSet.inter). So μ-a.e. x lies in M₁ ∩ M₂ (ae_restrict_mem₀). For such x, x ∈ M₂, so θ₂(x) > 0 (field pos of the second triple); in particular θ₂(x) ≠ 0.

2. (Frames from both orientation conditions.)
   - The field orients of the first triple holds H.restrict M₁-a.e., hence μ-a.e. because M₁ ∩ M₂ ⊆ M₁ (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset). It gives an orthonormal τ¹ : Fin n → ℝ^P with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₁ θ₁ x (span(range τ¹)) and ξ₁(x) = s(τ¹) or ξ₁(x) = −s(τ¹).
   - Likewise, using M₁ ∩ M₂ ⊆ M₂, μ-a.e. there is an orthonormal τ² with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₂ θ₂ x (span(range τ²)) and ξ₂(x) = ±s(τ²).

3. (Equal spans.)
   - Intersect the μ-a.e. statements of steps 1–2 with the hypothesis (filter_upwards), and fix such an x.
   - The hypothesis with Q := span(range τ¹) shows that span(range τ¹) is also a weighted approximate tangent space of (M₂, θ₂) at x.
   - Since θ₂(x) ≠ 0, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique gives span(range τ¹) = span(range τ²).

4. (Combine the signs.)
   - The sibling frame_sign with τ := τ¹, τ' := τ² gives s(τ²) = ε·s(τ¹) with ε ∈ {1, −1}.
   - Write ξ₁(x) = ε₁·s(τ¹) and ξ₂(x) = ε₂·s(τ²) with ε₁, ε₂ ∈ {1, −1}.
   - Then ξ₂(x) = ε₂ε·s(τ¹), so s(τ¹) = ε₂ε·ξ₂(x) because (ε₂ε)² = 1.
   - Hence ξ₁(x) = ε₁ε₂ε·ξ₂(x) with ε₁ε₂ε ∈ {1, −1}, i.e. ξ₁(x) = ξ₂(x) or ξ₁(x) = −ξ₂(x). This is an eight-case check using neg_neg. ∎
proof_key_steps: μ-a.e. x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ has θ₂(x) > 0 and orthonormal frames τ¹, τ² from the two orientation conditions
the hypothesis makes span τ¹ a weighted tangent space of (M₂, θ₂); uniqueness gives span τ¹ = span τ²
frame_sign gives s(τ²) = ±s(τ¹); combining the signs gives ξ₁ = ±ξ₂

subproblems.title: Zero k-density off a carrier at all scales Rr (Upper Density Theorem, Simon Ch. 1, 3.6)
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, Hᵏ := μHE[k] on ℝ^P = Eucl P, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, S ⊆ ℝ^P Hᵏ-null-measurable, and g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] (not necessarily measurable) with ∫⁻_{S∩K} g dHᵏ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. Then for Hᵏ-almost every x with x ∈ U and x ∉ S, and for every R > 0, r^{−k}·∫⁻_{S ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x)} g dHᵏ → 0 as r ↓ 0 (r^{−k} is written ENNReal.ofReal((r^k)⁻¹), B̄_ρ(x) = closedBall x ρ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U S : Set (Eucl P)) (g : Eucl P → ℝ≥0∞), IsOpen U → NullMeasurableSet S (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl P)) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∫⁻ y in S ∩ K, g y ∂(μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl P)) < ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl P)), x ∈ U → x ∉ S → ∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal ((r ^ k)⁻¹) * ∫⁻ y in S ∩ closedBall x (R * r), g y ∂(μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl P))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P := Eucl P. H := Hᵏ := μHE[k], Mathlib's normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P. It is a Borel measure but in general not σ-finite, and "H-a.e." means outside a set of H-outer-measure 0. B̄_s(x) := closedBall x s and B_s(x) := ball x s. For r > 0, ofReal((r^k)⁻¹) = r^{−k}. For a Borel measure ν on ℝ^P, Θ*ᵏ(ν, x) := dimensionalUpperDensity ν.toOuterMeasure (k : ℝ) univ x, i.e. limsup_{s↓0} q(s) with q(s) := dimensionalDensityQuotient ν.toOuterMeasure k univ x s = ν(univ ∩ B̄_s(x)) / (ω_k · ofReal(s)^(k : ℝ)) = ν(B̄_s(x)) / (ω_k · ofReal(s)^k), where ω_k := realUnitBallVolume k ∈ (0, ∞) (SimonGMT). Countable unions of H-null sets are H-null.

Source. This is preliminary (iv) of the parent proof: Simon Ch. 1, 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2), the upper density theorem. Here it is derived from the sibling `rectifiability_density_comparison` (Simon Ch. 1, 3.3: if V is open, A ⊆ V and t ≤ Θ*ᵏ(ν, x) for all x ∈ A, then t·H(A) ≤ ν(V)) and from outer regularity of finite Borel measures. This replaces the textbook covering argument.

Statement. Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and S ⊆ ℝ^P be H-null-measurable. Let g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] satisfy ∫⁻_{S∩K} g dH < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; g need not be measurable. Then for H-a.e. x with x ∈ U and x ∉ S, and for every R > 0: r^{−k} ∫⁻_{S ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x)} g dH → 0 as r ↓ 0.

1. (Countable cover by relatively compact balls.)
   - If U = ∅ there is nothing to prove.
   - The open balls B_s(y) with s > 0 and B̄_s(y) ⊆ U cover U, since U is open.
   - ℝ^P is second countable, so countably many of them, W_i := B_{s_i}(y_i) (i ∈ ℕ), still cover U (Lindelöf; Mathlib `TopologicalSpace.isOpen_sUnion_countable`, or `isOpen_iUnion_countable`).
   - K_i := B̄_{s_i}(y_i) is compact, because closed bounded sets of ℝ^P are compact (`isCompact_closedBall`), and W_i ⊆ K_i ⊆ U.
   - The exceptional set of the claim is contained in the union over i of the exceptional sets of the claim restricted to x ∈ W_i. So it suffices to fix i and prove: for H-a.e. x ∈ W_i ∖ S and every R > 0, the convergence holds. Write W := W_i and K := K_i.

2. (A finite measure carried by S ∩ K.)
   - Let ν := (H⌞(S ∩ K)).withDensity g. So ν(B) = ∫⁻_{B} g d(H⌞(S∩K)) = ∫⁻_{B ∩ (S ∩ K)} g dH for every Borel set B (`withDensity_apply`, `Measure.restrict_restrict`).
   - Then ν(ℝ^P) = ∫⁻_{S∩K} g dH < ∞, so ν is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P.
   - Let x ∈ W and s > 0 with B̄_s(x) ⊆ W. Then B̄_s(x) ∩ S ∩ K = S ∩ B̄_s(x), because W ⊆ K. Hence ν(B̄_s(x)) = ∫⁻_{S ∩ B̄_s(x)} g dH.

3. (ν does not charge the complement of S.)
   - S is H-null-measurable, so there is a measurable S₀ ⊆ S with H(S ∖ S₀) = 0 (`NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq`).
   - T := ℝ^P ∖ S₀ is measurable and contains ℝ^P ∖ S.
   - ν(T) = ∫⁻_{T ∩ (S ∩ K)} g dH = 0, because T ∩ S ∩ K ⊆ S ∖ S₀ is H-null (a lintegral over an H-null set vanishes, `setLIntegral_measure_zero`).

4. (Outer regularity.)
   - A finite Borel measure on a metric space is outer regular (Mathlib: `MeasureTheory.Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure`, so `OuterRegular`).
   - Hence for every η > 0 there is an open V ⊇ T with ν(V) < ν(T) + η = η (`Set.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt` / `MeasurableSet.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt`).

5. (Density comparison.)
   - Fix t ∈ (0, ∞) and put A_t := {x ∈ W : x ∉ S and t ≤ Θ*ᵏ(ν, x)}.
   - Given η > 0, take V from step 4 and put V′ := V ∩ W. This is open, and A_t ⊆ V′ because A_t ⊆ W ∖ S ⊆ T ⊆ V.
   - The sibling `rectifiability_density_comparison`, applied to ν, A := A_t, V := V′ and t, gives t·H(A_t) ≤ ν(V′) ≤ ν(V) < η.
   - As η > 0 was arbitrary, t·H(A_t) = 0, and since t ≠ 0, H(A_t) = 0.

6. (Zero density almost everywhere.)
   - If x ∈ W ∖ S and Θ*ᵏ(ν, x) ≠ 0, then 1/m ≤ Θ*ᵏ(ν, x) for some integer m ≥ 1 (`ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt`), so x ∈ A_{1/m}.
   - By step 5 and countable subadditivity, Θ*ᵏ(ν, x) = 0 for H-a.e. x ∈ W ∖ S.

7. (From zero density to the normalized integral.) Fix x ∈ W ∖ S with Θ*ᵏ(ν, x) = 0, and fix R > 0.
   - The quotients q(s) ∈ [0, ∞] satisfy limsup_{s↓0} q(s) = 0. Since q ≥ 0, this means q(s) → 0 as s ↓ 0 (in a complete linear order, limsup = ⊥ forces convergence to ⊥).
   - The map r ↦ Rr sends 𝓝[>] 0 to 𝓝[>] 0 (R > 0). Hence q(Rr) → 0 as r ↓ 0.
   - For r > 0 so small that B̄_{Rr}(x) ⊆ W (possible since W is open and x ∈ W), step 2 gives
     r^{−k} ∫⁻_{S ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x)} g dH = r^{−k} ν(B̄_{Rr}(x)) = (ω_k · R^k) · q(Rr).
     Here ofReal(Rr)^k = R^k r^k and 0 < ω_k R^k < ∞.
   - Hence r^{−k} ∫⁻_{S ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x)} g dH → (ω_k R^k) · 0 = 0 as r ↓ 0 (`ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul`, since ω_k R^k ≠ ∞).
   - The identity holds eventually in 𝓝[>] 0, which suffices (`Tendsto.congr'`).

8. (Conclusion.) By steps 6–7 the claim holds for H-a.e. x ∈ W_i ∖ S, for every i. By step 1 it holds for H-a.e. x ∈ U ∖ S. That is, for H-a.e. x: x ∈ U → x ∉ S → ∀ R > 0, the convergence holds. ∎

- x ↦ (θ(x) • ξ(x))(ω(x)) is H⌞M-integrable; and
- X(ω) = ∫ (θ(x) • ξ(x))(ω(x)) d(H⌞M)(x).

1. (The test form.) Fix ω ∈ D^k(U) and write ω also for its underlying form ℝ^P → Λᵏ(ℝ^P).

Statement. Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and M ⊆ U be H-null-measurable, with H(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be H-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U. Then for H⌞M-a.e. x and every R > 0:
  r^{−k} ∫⁻_{M ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x)} ‖f(y) − f(x)‖ₑ dH(y) → 0 as r ↓ 0.

1. (Countable cover by relatively compact balls.)
   - If U = ∅ then M = ∅ and H⌞M = 0, so there is nothing to prove.
   - The balls B_s(y) with s > 0 and B̄_s(y) ⊆ U cover U. By second countability of ℝ^P, countably many of them, W_i := B_{s_i}(y_i) (i ∈ ℕ), cover U (`TopologicalSpace.isOpen_sUnion_countable`).
   - K_i := B̄_{s_i}(y_i) is compact with W_i ⊆ K_i ⊆ U.
   - Since M ⊆ U = ⋃_i W_i, and a countable union of H⌞M-null sets is H⌞M-null, it suffices to fix i and prove the claim for H⌞M-a.e. x ∈ W_i. Write W := W_i and K := K_i.

2. (A finite measure.)
   - λ := H⌞(M ∩ K) is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P, since λ(ℝ^P) = H(M ∩ K) < ∞.
   - f is λ-integrable, by the hypothesis with this K.
   - For x ∈ W and s > 0 with B̄_s(x) ⊆ W ⊆ K: λ(B̄_s(x)) = H(M ∩ B̄_s(x)), and ∫⁻_{B̄_s(x)} ‖f − f(x)‖ₑ dλ = ∫⁻_{M ∩ B̄_s(x)} ‖f − f(x)‖ₑ dH. Here λ⌞B̄_s(x) = H⌞(B̄_s(x) ∩ M ∩ K) by `Measure.restrict_restrict` (closed balls are measurable), and B̄_s(x) ∩ M ∩ K = M ∩ B̄_s(x).

3. (Lebesgue–Besicovitch differentiation.)
   - λ is finite, hence locally finite and s-finite, and ℝ^P has the Besicovitch covering property (finite-dimensional normed space).
   - Apply Mathlib's `VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div` to the Vitali family `Besicovitch.vitaliFamily λ` and the λ-integrable (hence locally integrable) f. Compose with `Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt λ x`: closed balls B̄_s(x), s ↓ 0, tend to the Vitali filter at x.
   - This gives a λ-null set N such that for every x ∉ N:
     a_x(s) := (∫⁻_{B̄_s(x)} ‖f − f(x)‖ₑ dλ) / λ(B̄_s(x)) → 0 as s ↓ 0.
   - λ(N) = 0 means H(N ∩ M ∩ K) = 0, since M ∩ K is null-measurable (`Measure.restrict_apply₀'`). Hence H⌞M(N ∩ W) = 0.

4. (Finite upper density.)
   - Let A_∞ := {x ∈ W : Θ*ᵏ(λ, x) = ∞}.
   - For every real t > 0: A_∞ ⊆ W, W is open, and t ≤ Θ*ᵏ(λ, x) for x ∈ A_∞. The sibling `rectifiability_density_comparison` gives t·H(A_∞) ≤ λ(W) ≤ λ(ℝ^P) < ∞.
   - If H(A_∞) > 0, then t·H(A_∞) > λ(ℝ^P) for all large real t (also when H(A_∞) = ∞), a contradiction. So H(A_∞) = 0, hence H⌞M(A_∞) = 0.

5. (Good points.) Let x ∈ M ∩ W with x ∉ N ∪ A_∞, and fix R > 0.
   - Θ*ᵏ(λ, x) < ∞, so choose a real C > 0 with Θ*ᵏ(λ, x) < C. By the definition of limsup (`Filter.eventually_lt_of_limsup_lt`), eventually for s ↓ 0, λ(B̄_s(x))/(ω_k s^k) < C, i.e. λ(B̄_s(x)) ≤ C ω_k s^k.
   - Since Rr ↓ 0 as r ↓ 0 and W is open, for all sufficiently small r > 0 the radius s := Rr satisfies both this bound and B̄_s(x) ⊆ W.
   - For such r, put I(r) := ∫⁻_{M ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x)} ‖f − f(x)‖ₑ dH = ∫⁻_{B̄_s(x)} ‖f − f(x)‖ₑ dλ (step 2). Then I(r) ≤ λ(B̄_s(x)) · a_x(s):
     · if 0 < λ(B̄_s(x)) < ∞, this is an equality by the definition of a_x(s) (`ENNReal.div_mul_cancel`);
     · if λ(B̄_s(x)) = 0, then λ⌞B̄_s(x) = 0 and I(r) = 0.
   - Therefore r^{−k} I(r) ≤ r^{−k} · C ω_k (Rr)^k · a_x(Rr) = (C ω_k R^k) · a_x(Rr).
   - The right side tends to (C ω_k R^k) · 0 = 0 as r ↓ 0. This is step 3 composed with r ↦ Rr, which maps 𝓝[>] 0 to 𝓝[>] 0, together with `ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul`, using C ω_k R^k ≠ ∞.
   - By the squeeze theorem in [0, ∞] (`tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le'`, lower bound 0), r^{−k} I(r) → 0.

6. (Conclusion.) By steps 3–4, H⌞M-a.e. x ∈ W is a good point in the sense of step 5. By step 1 the claim holds for H⌞M-a.e. x. ∎

subproblems.title: Restrictions of integer multiplicity currents are integer multiplicity, given tangent comparison
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, Hᵏ := μHE[k] on ℝ^P = Eucl P, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and assume the tangent comparison principle (T) in U: for all Hᵏ-null-measurable M₁, M₂ ⊆ U and all θ₁, θ₂ : ℝ^P → ℝ with θ_l(x) ≥ 1 for x ∈ M_l and θ_l Hᵏ-integrable on M_l ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U (l = 1, 2), for Hᵏ⌞(M₁ ∩ M₂)-almost every x, every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P that is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M₁, θ₁) at x (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M₁ θ₁ x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.7) is also one of (M₂, θ₂) at x (the parent obtains (T) from the sibling iwl_imc_tangent_overlap applied to iwl_weighted_tangent_locality P k and U; this child takes (T) as a hypothesis and does not use that sibling). Then for every integer multiplicity X ∈ D_k(U) (IsIntegerMultiplicity X), every A ⊆ ℝ^P and every S ∈ D_k(U) with IsRestriction X A S (S = X⌞A, Simon Ch. 6, 2.9), S is integer multiplicity.

Conventions. ℝ^P := Eucl P and H := Hᵏ := μHE[k]. D_k(U) := GeometricCurrentOn U k and D^k(U) := TestFormOn U k. τ(M, θ, ξ)(ω) := tauAction k M θ ξ ω = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH(x). Statement. Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and assume (T). If X ∈ D_k(U) is i.m., A ⊆ ℝ^P and S ∈ D_k(U) satisfy IsRestriction X A S, then S is i.m.

   - X is i.m., so there are M, θ, ξ with IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ, θ(x) ∈ ℕ for x ∈ M, and X(ω) = τ(M, θ, ξ)(ω) for every ω ∈ D^k(U).

2. (A second representation.) By the sibling `iwl_imc_tau_measure_representation`, (H⌞M, θ • ξ) is a measure representation of X.

3. (Restriction formula, parent step (b)1.) Apply the sibling `slicing_representation_unique` with U (open), μ₁ := μ, v₁ := v, μ₂ := H⌞M, v₂ := θ • ξ, and W := U (open). Its hypotheses hold:

     S(ω) = ∫_A v(ω) dμ = ∫_A (θ • ξ)(ω) d(H⌞M).

   - subset: M ∩ A ⊆ M ⊆ U.

   - countablyRectifiable: M ∩ A ⊆ M (`CountablyRectifiable.mono`).
   - pos: θ > 0 on M ∩ A ⊆ M.
   - integrableOn: for compact K ⊆ U, (M ∩ A) ∩ K ⊆ M ∩ K and θ is integrable on M ∩ K (`IntegrableOn.mono_set`).
   - aestronglyMeasurable: H⌞(M ∩ A) ≤ H⌞M (`Measure.restrict_mono`), so ξ stays a.e.-strongly measurable (`AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure`).
   - orients:
     · Apply (T) with (M₁′, θ₁′) := (M, θ) and (M₂′, θ₂′) := (M ∩ A, θ). Its hypotheses are the fields just listed together with θ ≥ 1 on M ⊇ M ∩ A.
     · Since M ∩ (M ∩ A) = M ∩ A, for H⌞(M ∩ A)-a.e. x every weighted tangent space of (M, θ) at x is one of (M ∩ A, θ) at x.
     · The field `orients` of (M, θ, ξ) holds H⌞M-a.e., hence H⌞(M ∩ A)-a.e. (`ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset`).
